content.title: About
content.content: Bacon NS is a smoked pork bacon with reduced sodium, prepared by dry heat treatment (685). It offers the classic smoky aroma, tender flavor, and crisp texture while containing significantly less salt than regular bacon.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bacon NS is made from selected pork belly cuts that are brined with a low‑sodium solution.
The 685 °C heat treatment creates a crunchy crust without the need for extra salt.
Reduced sodium makes the product more suitable for people monitoring their salt intake.
Bacon NS is often used in diet menus where flavor balance and salt restriction are important.
When stored properly, the bacon retains its quality for up to 12 months.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Bacon NS provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports the nervous system and the formation of red blood cells.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Reduced salt helps maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Bacon NS offers a quick source of energy from fats, though the fat content is moderated compared with regular bacon.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Despite lower sodium, bacon still contains saturated fats and should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to pork may experience reactions.

items.title: Nitrate content
items.content: Like most smoked products, bacon may contain small amounts of nitrates, which should be limited with frequent consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bacon NS can be pan‑fried, baked in the oven, or microwaved until crisp. Use it in salads, sandwiches, egg dishes, or as a flavorful topping for vegetable sides.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store Bacon NS in its original packaging in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. After opening, tightly wrap in cling film or place in an airtight container. When frozen, it retains quality for up to 6 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Black beans and rice is a popular fast‑food dish that combines cooked black beans with fluffy rice, often served with sauce, spices, and vegetables. The meal is rich in plant protein, fiber, and carbohydrates, making it filling and nutritious.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black beans (Phaseolus vulgaris) originated in South America and have been used by indigenous peoples for over 7,000 years.
The bean‑rice combination is considered a complete protein source because the amino acid profiles complement each other.
In the United States the dish is frequently offered as a “bowl” in fast‑food chains, topped with guacamole, cheese, and salsa.
Black beans get their deep color from anthocyanins, which are powerful antioxidants.
The traditional Mexican version “arroz con frijoles” often includes tomato sauce and chili spices.

items.title: High in plant protein
items.content: Black beans provide about 8 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for blood formation and normal nerve function.

items.title: Low glycemic index rice option
items.content: When paired with brown rice, the dish raises blood glucose slowly, which is beneficial for weight management.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Anthocyanins in black beans help combat free radicals and reduce inflammation.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans, ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can impair mineral absorption; soaking beans before cooking reduces this effect.

items.title: High sodium in sauces
items.content: Restaurant sauces often contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause gastrointestinal gas in sensitive people; gradual introduction to the diet can lessen the issue.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, typically in a bowl or tray. Top with guacamole, sour cream, shredded cheese, fresh salsa, or a squeeze of lime for extra flavor. It pairs well with corn chips or a side salad of fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in the microwave or on a skillet, adding a splash of water to prevent drying out.

chicken-or-turkey-potatoes-and-vegetable.title: Chicken or Turkey with Potatoes and Vegetables (No Sauce)

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of roasted or boiled chicken or turkey, potatoes and vegetables (carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens). It is prepared without added sauces, preserving the natural flavors of the ingredients and making it easy to digest.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are complete protein sources containing all essential amino acids.
Potatoes are one of the world’s most consumed root vegetables; they are rich in starch and vitamin C.
Broccoli is considered a “super‑vegetable” because of its high levels of vitamins C, K and folate.
Dark‑green leafy greens (spinach, kale, collard greens) are packed with iron and antioxidants.
The absence of sauce reduces added sugars and sodium, making the meal healthier.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Poultry meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C from potatoes and broccoli boosts the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Vitamin K and calcium from leafy greens help strengthen bones.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Fiber from vegetables and potatoes promotes healthy gut motility.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Phytonutrients in broccoli and leafy greens help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken or turkey.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: When using processed meat or seasonings, monitor added salt levels.

items.title: Potential pathogens
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor bacteria; ensure internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

items.title: Oxalates in leafy greens
items.content: People prone to kidney stones should consume spinach and kale in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main meal. It can be sliced into portions, added to salads, or used as a filling for wraps.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to 75 °C before eating.

content.title: About
content.content: Gluten free plain crackers are crisp, dry biscuits made from gluten‑free grains such as rice, corn or potato starch and a pinch of salt. They contain no wheat, barley or rye, making them suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity. Their neutral flavor makes them a versatile base for toppings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gluten‑free crackers are a staple in many low‑gluten diets because they pair well with a variety of spreads.
Rice flour is commonly used, giving the crackers a light, airy texture.
Because they lack gluten, they reduce the risk of allergic reactions in celiac individuals.
Plain crackers are often used in culinary schools to test new sauces and toppings.
Some brands add seeds (e.g., pumpkin) to boost flavor and nutritional value.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Most gluten‑free crackers are baked with minimal oil, making them less calorie‑dense than many traditional snacks.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Rice or corn‑based crackers provide slow‑releasing energy, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Suitable for individuals with celiac disease, gluten intolerance, or those following a gluten‑free diet.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: The neutral composition makes them a gentle option for those with digestive sensitivities.

items.title: Moderate sodium
items.content: A modest amount of salt helps maintain electrolyte balance without excessive sodium intake.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some gluten‑free crackers may contain soy, dairy or nuts, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rice‑based crackers can raise blood sugar quickly, which may be a concern for diabetics.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although usually moderate, people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Added additives
items.content: Certain brands use flavor enhancers such as monosodium glutamate, which some individuals prefer to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Gluten free crackers can be enjoyed plain, spread with hummus, cream cheese, avocado, or used as a base for canapés. They also add a crunchy topping to soups and salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in the sealed package. After opening, transfer to an airtight container to prevent moisture absorption. Follow the “best before” date on the packaging.

content.title: About
content.content: Duck is a waterfowl whose meat is prized for its rich flavor and darker color compared with chicken. In this preparation the skin is removed after roasting to reduce fat while retaining the meat’s high nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Duck meat contains more iron than chicken, making it a good source of this mineral.
Traditional Chinese Peking duck is served with crispy skin, but this version discards the skin for a leaner dish.
Duck meat is rich in collagen, which supports skin and joint health.
Although ducks can fly, the birds used for food are typically farm‑raised and flightless.
In many cultures duck is considered a festive delicacy.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Duck provides complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals help form hemoglobin and support immune function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Duck supplies B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Makes it suitable for low‑carb and keto diets.

items.title: Beneficial fatty acids
items.content: Even without skin, the meat retains omega‑3 and omega‑6 fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Bird allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to poultry meat.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Seasoning often adds salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Possible bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked duck can harbor salmonella or campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 74 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the skin‑less roasted duck thinly and add to salads, soups, rice or noodle dishes. It also works well as a filling for crepes or as a protein component in Asian‑style stir‑fries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0–4 °C for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag for up to 3 months. Reheat thoroughly to an internal temperature of 74 °C before serving.

egg-omelet-or-scrambled-egg-with-meat-an.title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with meat and dark‑green vegetables, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of eggs, lean meat (such as chicken breast or turkey) and dark‑green vegetables (spinach, broccoli, kale). No fat is added – it is cooked on a dry pan or in the microwave. Eggs provide high‑quality protein, meat adds extra protein and iron, and the greens supply vitamins, minerals and fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most nutrient‑dense foods, containing all essential amino acids.
Dark‑green vegetables are rich in chlorophyll, which may support body detoxification.
Cooking without added fat preserves the natural taste of the ingredients and lowers the calorie count.
The combination of protein and fiber helps keep you feeling full longer.
The dish is quick to prepare, making it a popular breakfast or light‑lunch option.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Eggs and meat together provide about 25‑30 g of protein per serving, supporting muscle and tissue maintenance.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and meat supply vitamin B12, while the greens provide folate (B9), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of iron and zinc
items.content: Lean meat and spinach deliver easily absorbable iron and zinc, which support immune function.

items.title: Antioxidants and phytochemicals
items.content: Dark‑green vegetables contain lutein, zeaxanthin and vitamin K, beneficial for eye health and bone strength.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: The absence of added fat keeps the dish light: roughly 250‑300 kcal per serving.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg white proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Processed meat concerns
items.content: Choose lean, minimally processed meat to avoid excess sodium and additives.

items.title: Oxalates in spinach
items.content: Large amounts of spinach can increase the risk of kidney stones in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Beat the eggs, add finely chopped meat and pre‑cooked or lightly steamed dark‑green vegetables. Pour the mixture onto a hot dry pan, cook over medium heat, stirring until the desired consistency is reached. Season with pepper, paprika or herbs if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The dish is best eaten fresh. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat on a dry pan or in the microwave.

content.title: About
content.content: Ensure Plus is a ready‑to‑drink nutritional shake designed to support daily energy and nutrient needs. It provides a balanced blend of protein, carbohydrates, fats, vitamins, minerals, and extra calories, making it a convenient way to supplement the diet.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The product is sold in more than 30 countries worldwide.
Each serving delivers about 350 kcal, useful for weight gain or high energy expenditure.
It contains probiotics that support digestive health.
Ensure Plus has a neutral flavor that appeals to both adults and children.
Long shelf life makes it convenient for travel and office use.

items.title: Energy balance support
items.content: A mix of fast‑ and slow‑release carbohydrates provides immediate and sustained energy.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Each serving supplies about 10 g of protein, helping maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Vitamin‑mineral complex
items.content: Includes B‑vitamins, vitamin D, calcium, iron, and zinc essential for normal body functions.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C and zinc contribute to a healthy immune system.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The formula is designed to be gentle on the gastrointestinal tract, even when food intake is limited.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The product contains dairy protein; individuals with an allergy should avoid it.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: People with diabetes or who limit sugar should consult a healthcare professional before use.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Regular consumption in large amounts may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Lactose content
items.content: Those with lactose intolerance may need to choose an alternative product.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: The shake is ready to drink straight from the bottle. It can be enjoyed cold or slightly warmed, added to smoothies, or used as a base for protein cocktails.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 7 days.

white-pizza-cheese-thin-crust.title: White Pizza with Cheese, Thin Crust

content.title: About
content.content: White pizza with cheese on a thin crust is a classic Italian snack without tomato sauce. The crisp thin dough is topped with a blend of creamy cheese, mozzarella and sometimes parmesan, plus aromatic herbs. It bakes quickly at high heat, preserving the delicate cheese flavor and light texture of the crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The traditional “white” pizza (Pizza Bianca) originated in Naples as a way to use leftover cheese and butter after making tomato‑based pies.
Thin crust allows for even baking and gives the pizza a characteristic crunchy edge.
Creamy cheeses such as ricotta are often added to white pizza for a richer texture.
In some regions garlic or rosemary is sprinkled on top to boost aroma.
White pizza is usually served without tomato sauce, making it lighter in taste and calories.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The cheeses used in the pizza are rich in calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Mozzarella and other cheeses provide complete protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Dairy products are a good source of vitamin B12, supporting the nervous system.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Absence of tomato sauce reduces simple sugars in the dish.

items.title: Potential probiotics (when using fermented cheeses)
items.content: Certain cheeses like parmesan can contribute to a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheeses contain lactose, which may cause discomfort for those who are intolerant.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheeses are often salty, so people monitoring salt intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to milk proteins.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Thin crust and cheese make the pizza relatively calorie‑dense; moderation is advised.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional crust contains gluten, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pizza hot, sliced into portions. Fresh basil, arugula, or a drizzle of olive oil add brightness. Pair with a green salad for a balanced meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore the crisp crust.
